title: Grateful Dead Live at Fox Theatre on 1970-02-02
lineage: SBD > MR > R > R > PCM > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a legendary early‑1970 show highlighted by an epic Dark Star and superb St. Stephen → Mason’s Children transition.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crisp, high‑fidelity SBD that showcases the band at a creative peak in early ’70. Reviewers rave about the 20‑minute Dark Star, the tight interplay between Garcia and Lesh, and the seamless segue into a rare Mason’s Children, while noting the inevitable frustration of the truncated source. Overall the performance is described as inspired, fiery and one of the most compelling snapshots of this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed reviews uniformly praise both the musical performance (especially Dark Star) and the soundboard quality, with only minor complaints about the recording’s brevity.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly call the SBD "crisp", "sonic quality excellent" and "great sounding"; the only technical drawback is the abrupt cut of Mason's Children due to the source being an excerpt.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised for its high‑energy, exploratory vibe of early ’70; the highlight is the fluid transition from St. Stephen into Mason’s Children, underscoring a period when the band was "clearly on a roll".

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's solo is described as "smoking", "perfect tone" and one of his most emphatic Dark Star performances.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass work is noted as inspired and part of a “perfect” band that was firing on all cylinders.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir gets credit for shining moments within the long Dark Star jam.
